I’ll attach the E2E Long (experimental mode) graphs included in the pull request here for record-keeping.
The x-axis represents time, and the y-axis represents the accelerator command (desired acceleration).
Positive values indicate acceleration, while negative values indicate deceleration (braking).
Since openpilot runs at 20 Hz, 60 frames correspond to approximately 3 seconds.

v12 looks like a more speed-stable model, as the acceleration curve after applying throttle is much smoother, resulting in more consistent and steady speed control.
I’m really looking forward to driving it in the real world!

I’ve driven so far 5 miles, and the long is amazing. Might even get me a speeding ticket if I’m not careful with setting the top speed 😂. I think it has reached a point where it feels better than my stock VW long, but I need more seat time. 

Downsides so far:
tries to go too fast at roundabouts.

Not complaining; I’d rather have this problem rather than it being too slow and me getting tailgated.

I drove the WMI v12 model in experimental mode for about 30 minutes at night.
This was a nighttime test on public roads, using a comma four.

The E2E longitudinal behavior in experimental mode felt smoother and more confident than any previous WMI model I’ve tried, even at night. Acceleration and deceleration feel very deliberate and controlled. It smoothly accelerates up to the driver-set speed and smoothly slows down for lead vehicles.
It was honestly an excellent nighttime driving experience—zero stress around accel/decel. Really impressive work.

Lateral control is also very strong. It generally feels well-centered, though on narrow roads at night I occasionally felt it was positioned slightly closer to the driver-side lane. This may be related to the nighttime conditions.

In my specific environment, I think it’s better to avoid using Dynamic Experimental Control (DEC).
At least in my setup, I’ve found the system to be significantly more stable when using only WMI v12 in experimental mode.
With chill mode, the car tries to strictly maintain the set speed, so in scenarios like the one shown in the video, it tends to keep a higher speed and may slip as a result.
Additionally, in my experience, the automatic switching between chill mode and experimental mode in DEC often does not work as intended.

Well, after extended usage on Experimental Mode only:

Long - Highway: EXCELLENT on Highway. It actually stays at speed with traffic at 75-80 MPH. Gap is much closer than any model before. There are moments where when traffic slows down the model doesn’t speed up in time but it’s not as irritating as previous model. 

Long - City: Not so great here. It will stop and roll through red lights and stop signs. Gap between cars are closer, but not steady when the model hesitates with traffic slowing down and the gap gets bigger and bigger. 

Lateral: overall, great on highway. 

I think it hugs a bit in city but nothing outrageous. I’m okay with lateral except for 90 degree turns, the turning is jittery compared to previous models that unwind a lot more smoothly.

Tried it out with experimental mode only, on the highway and in the town. I feel like at lower speeds, the steering wheel jitter is pretty high.
It seems to keep the speed pretty well on the highway. Sometimes going above the speed limit, but randomly going 5-10km/h below the speed limit with no one in front of me.
In the city, I got a lot more of the messages to take the wheel than normal. I don't feel like it was taking the corners too much. But I'm not sure. It cut one corner a bit too much and there was another car in the other direction. But the default model also cuts this corner. It was just even more aggressive this time.
In the city, a few times it slowed down for a corner, 40km/h for example, and then didn't speed up again after the corner.

I’ve been consistently above 70% engagement on my commutes (attached best one yet). And haven’t gone back to Chill. 

I usually average around 46% engagement. The most I’ve gotten is 55% on a good day (no crazy traffic) using Chill, so this is a big improvement for me.

The issues I’m seeing (which mostly end up with me disengaging):

Stopping for lights or stop signs:
- It doesn’t stop consistently. By this, I mean it sometimes will apply brakes too late or not hard enough, and if I don’t intervene, it stops 3-4 ft into the white line. 
- If it does stop, it creeps a few inches forward, then a few more, and more… I end up intervening at that point. Interestingly enough, if I activate it during a red light, it has no issue waiting. (Did have one occasion when it seemed like it was going to take off though.) 

Lead distance 
- In heavy traffic scenarios where the lead slows down and then accelerates, Comma will not accelerate fast enough to keep up. Ex. Traffic just cleared up, and the lead goes from 30 mph to 70 mph, I’m still chilling at 35-40 with no further acceleration happening. 

I don’t doubt it will eventually catch on, but being where I am… I end up overriding the gas before I get someone road raging behind me. 

Phantom braking in shadows. 
- Not as bad as Tesla but still annoying. There’s a rural road that in the evening, trees cast multiple shadows that look like  black lines on the road. Comma basically becomes useless (slows down too much). Had this same problem with FSD, so I’m not phased by it. 

Rubber banding
- It does not happen a lot, but when it does, it’s annoying AF. If you have a lead car that can’t keep a constant speed, you’ll end up getting close to them. Comma slows down maybe 2-3 mph under the lead, then the lead takes off, and Comma happily accelerates only for it to happen all over again. 

Turns
- Seems like it can’t calculate the lead well in turns, and sometimes it gets too close to the car in front only to suddenly slow down. 

Left side bias
- sometimes it just wants to ride the left side line. I can reposition it and it will go back in 3 seconds. I’ve found that disengaging and engaging again fixes this.
